sentences.text: In textbooks, wires have zero resistance, capacitors have zero inductance, and ground is an equipotential plane.
In real hardware, every trace has parasitic resistance and inductance, and digital switching generates fast current spikes.
Rule One: Always place a 0.1 microfarad ceramic bypass capacitor as close as physically possible to the power pin of every IC chip.
This supplies local high-frequency current pulses without voltage droop across long PCB traces.
Rule Two: Use a continuous, unbroken Ground Plane on 2-layer and 4-layer PCBs to minimize ground loop area and EMI noise.
Rule Three: Never leave high-impedance CMOS inputs floating.
Always pull them up or down with a 10k resistor.
strong>Horowitz & Hill Pro-Tip: The #1 reason microcontroller and op-amp boards glitch, reset intermittently, or oscillate is missing decoupling capacitors.
Place a 100nF (0.1µF) X7R ceramic cap at every single power pin!
